user.title: ELM327 Bluetooth LE adapter
user.description: Pick the OBD-II adapter plugged into the car. Only adapters Home Assistant can hear right now are listed, and the car must be within reach of a Bluetooth proxy.

error.cannot_connect: Couldn't connect to the adapter, or it didn't answer like an ELM327. Is the phone app still connected to it?

abort.already_configured: This adapter is already set up.

data.poll_interval: Battery voltage read every (seconds) while parked

data_description.vehicle: Some cars offer more than standard OBD-II, such as tyre pressures. Pick yours to read those too: the commands come from OBDb, the open vehicle signal database, and only the Mazda CX-9 has been tested with this integration. A car not listed can be typed as its OBDb repository name, like Mazda-CX-9.
data_description.running_voltage: The car is only asked for OBD data while the battery voltage is at least this, i.e. while the alternator is charging.
data_description.poll_interval: Reading the voltage only talks to the adapter, not the car. This is also how quickly an engine start is noticed.

year.title: Model year
year.description: Some of the {vehicle}'s readings differ between model years, so pick yours.

error.download_failed: Couldn't download that car's signal set from OBDb. Check the name matches an OBDb repository and that Home Assistant can reach GitHub.
error.no_readings: OBDb has nothing for that car this integration can read yet.

distance_with_mil.name: Distance with check engine light on
